checks.item: Independent search for misses by a different method
checks.evidence: Over all 3,347 kept extras vs all field_dev/test photos I ran (a) crop-tolerant gray correlation (extra crop 100/80/60/70% vs ref crop 100/80/60/70%, 8 rotations and flips, so 90-degree rotations included) and (b) Sobel edge-map correlation. Viewed the top 32 crop pairs (scores 0.807-0.882) and the top 8 edge pairs (0.62-0.72): 0 copies, all different photos of similar leaves/fruit. Contrast the previous build, where the same search found 7 easy copies in its top 30. Only the top 32 were viewed, so this is evidence of rarity, not zero.

I sampled 28 images dropped by the crop step (from the 1,066 in the ffca1d8 manifest that are absent now; 20 random plus 8 corn) and ran the repo's crop_scores on CPU to get each one's matched dev/test photo, then viewed all 28 pairs. True copies: 2 of 28 (apple rust google_0220 vs 'Apple rust leaf/774bc3595daf.jpg', 45 inliers; tomato late blight 177 vs a tomato plant photo, 150 inliers). The other 26 are different photos of similar content (cosine 0.80-0.93, 8-28 inliers, mostly corn, raspberry, grape, strawberry leaves). Over-removal is therefore high: about 90% of what the DINOv2 cosine rule removes in this sample is not a copy (small sample; 95% bounds roughly 80-98%). The sample is from the diff against the previous manifest, not a draw from all 2,173, so it is indicative.

Yes, they are: corn Gray_leaf_spot 17, Common_rust 23, Northern_Leaf_Blight 20 kept (field_train 65/115/132); versus ffca1d8, the crop step alone dropped 91/73/62 of the corn disease extras there, and 7 of my 8 sampled corn drops were different corn photos. docs/extra-sources.md already says this ('The crop-aware step dropped many corn photos because DINOv2 scores close-ups of corn leaves as similar to each other') and the 'thin classes' section says corn gains little. It is a training-data cost, honestly reported, not a leak. Corn_healthy 69 and Potato_healthy 178 still add classes with no field photos.

3,347 rows, split only extra_train, sha1 unique, groups all 'x' prefixed with 0 shared with field.csv or lab.csv, 0 sha1 shared with field. docs/extra-sources.md per-class table: 33 rows, 0 mismatches against the manifest and field.csv; sources v1 3,332 + v2 15; class_map n_kept sum 3,347; max per class 200 and one class at 200 (Apple healthy), as the doc says. Removal-step counts (2,173 crop step etc.) come from the build; I did not rerun the GPU build, but the rule applied to a CPU sample gave consistent results.

notes: Scoped recheck at d1b6c9b (merge of build into task/T4.5 after 86159db): git diff 86159db d1b6c9b shows no change to extra_train.csv, class_map_extra.csv, crop_copies.py, copy_check.py, extra_sources.py, tests/test_extra_sources.py or docs/extra-sources.md; docs/DECISIONS.md has no conflict markers, no heading lost from either side (T4.5 side and build side compared by ### headings), and no line removed relative to 86159db; fast tests 13 passed, 2 deselected. Earlier checks at 86159db stand. Residual copies are possible: my search viewed the top 32 crop-correlation and top 8 edge pairs and found none, which is evidence that easy copies are gone but not a zero. The doc's own bound (0 of 20 sampled in the 1,349 near-rule pool, up to about 14%, so up to about 190 extras by the 95% bound, though the point estimate is near zero and a cropped copy that I could not find with two independent measures is hard to spot) is the honest estimate. Impact on E12: even if a few dozen of the 3,347 extras were copies, they would be spread over disease classes with 15-70 field_dev photos each and 3,347 vs about 2,070 field_train, so a copy that matters would have to hit a specific dev photo; the likely effect is a fraction of a point of macro-F1 at most, but it cannot be excluded. A bigger issue for E12 is the opposite: the rule removes about 90% non-copies in my sample, so corn disease classes keep only 17-23 extras (healthy corn 69), which limits what E12 can show for corn. This is reported in the docs and decisions. 90-degree rotated crops are covered by my search (not by the shipped crop check), and none were found. The sample of over-removal comes from images that were kept in the previous build and dropped now, not from a uniform draw over all 2,173. I could not run `cmd /c start /belownormal` (access denied in my sandbox), so my scoring ran at normal priority, one process at a time.
